conflicts.claim_a: P-1232 (J Affective Disorders 370:401-411, 2025): plasma exosomal lncRNA panel (LINC001380, ENST00000484033, ENST00000531087) discriminates MCI from healthy controls at AUC 0.700 (95% CI 0.641-0.760; sens 72.0%, spec 60.7%), with external target-gene validation (ATP2A2/PSEN1) AUC 0.695 in AddNeuroMed/GSE63060 (n=310 discovery; 184 external).
conflicts.claim_b: P-1254 (Experimental Gerontology 186:112355, 2024): plasma exosomal miR-483-5p alone discriminates MCI from age-matched controls at AUC 0.901 (sens 79.2%, spec 100%); miR-502-5p AUC 0.872 (n=72 ROC cohort drawn from 275 screened community elderly).
conflicts.description: CONFLICT (Actor-detected 2026-09-04, Critic-survived, candidate pending G4): two plasma-exosomal non-coding-RNA studies answer the same question - can an exosomal ncRNA panel detect MCI against healthy aging controls in community cohorts? - and their headline accuracies differ by 0.20 AUC, the largest unexplained within-class gap in the corpus fluid-biomarker lane. P-1232's three-lncRNA panel achieves 0.700 WITH external validation (target-gene AUC 0.695 in AddNeuroMed), while P-1254's single miRNA achieves 0.901 with 100% specificity on n=72. Both sides: plasma exosomal cargo (ultracentrifugation + qPCR/RNA-seq), T1 MCI_vs_HC, general population, cross-sectional community cohorts - all four deterministic gates pass and raw modality_subtype is literally equal (plasma_biomarkers). Architectural interpretation: the pair splits the corpus's exosomal-cargo philosophy between PANEL-SCALE DISCOVERY (RNA-seq genome-wide lncRNA screening, CI-bounded performance, external validation) and TARGETED-CANDIDATE TESTING (literature-preselected miRNAs, single-site ROC, no external validation, no CI). The 0.20 gap is plausibly small-sample optimism (n=72 vs n=310; 100% specificity at 24 MCI cases), case-ascertainment difference (MoCA-screened community register vs MMSE-stratified cases) and cargo-class difference (miRNA vs lncRNA) - but no corpus study reconciles them, and the falsifiable consequence is stated in resolution_note.
conflicts.task_equivalence: both classify community-dwelling MCI vs healthy elderly controls from plasma exosomal non-coding RNAs (T1, MCI_vs_HC)
conflicts.dataset_family_equivalence: Guangzhou community cohort + AddNeuroMed external vs Gansu community cohort - distinct sites, same community-dwelling elderly class
conflicts.modality_family: plasma exosomal ncRNA (lncRNA panel vs microRNA candidates)
conflicts.apparent_performance_gap: 0.20 AUC (0.700 vs 0.901) on the same task class
conflicts.resolution: Both findings can stand; the conflict asserts the corpus cannot yet say whether exosomal lncRNA panels underperform exosomal single-miRNA markers, or whether the gap is cohort/ascertainment/small-n artefact.
conflicts.resolution_note: Architectural interpretation: panel-scale discovery (RNA-seq, CI-bounded, externally validated, AUC 0.700) versus targeted-candidate testing (preselected miRNAs, single-site ROC, AUC 0.901 at n=72 with 100% specificity) are two exosomal-biomarker philosophies whose performance claims have never been reconciled within one cohort. Falsifiable consequence: a head-to-head exosomal lncRNA+miRNA panel on one community cohort (n>=300, externally validated) should land between the two claims; if miR-483-5p holds AUC >=0.85 under external validation, cargo class (miRNA vs lncRNA) is the operative variable; if it collapses toward 0.70, small-sample optimism and ascertainment were operative. Either outcome resolves the conflict; neither study is in the corpus.

readjudication_2026_09_27.quantity_a: Cross-sectional discrimination (in-sample ROC AUC) of a logistic combination of three plasma-exosomal lncRNAs, for MCI defined by education-specific MMSE cut-offs versus 1:1 age/sex-matched community controls aged >=60 (Guangzhou; qRT-PCR set of 150 v 150).
readjudication_2026_09_27.quantity_b: Cross-sectional discrimination (in-sample ROC AUC, no CI) of single plasma-exosomal miRNAs (miR-483-5p; miR-502-5p), for MCI defined by MoCA < 26 plus European-consortium criteria versus community controls over 65 who averaged about 4.8 years younger (Gansu; 24 v 24).
grounds: The two AUCs are for different predictors: a logistic combination of three exosomal lncRNAs (P-1232) and a single literature-preselected exosomal miRNA (P-1254). Neither study measures the other's markers, and a different predictor set is a different quantity under the rule (P-1232 p5 quote; P-1254 p1 and p2 quotes).
Neither study claims the ordering the other would refute. P-1232's only lncRNA-versus-miRNA remark concerns research scope, not accuracy, and P-1254 does not discuss lncRNAs (P-1232 p8 quote).

The population behind the shared 'MCI vs healthy controls' label differs. P-1232 defines MCI by education-specific MMSE cut-offs (mean MMSE 18.46) against matched controls; P-1254 defines it by MoCA < 26 (mean MoCA 20.37) against controls about 4.8 years younger (P-1232 p2 and p3 quotes; P-1254 p2 and p4 quotes).
The dataset-family gate fails (two distinct community cohorts) and no waiver is on record. The record's 'all four deterministic gates pass' contradicts its own dataset_equal: false.

If the quantities were the same, the estimates would be incompatible (non-overlapping uncertainty). The verdict therefore does not dismiss the gap as noise; it rests on the quantity difference (P-1232 p5 and P-1254 p1 quotes).
The record overstates P-1232's validation. The lncRNA panel was evaluated only in the Chinese sample, and the AddNeuroMed analysis tested ATP2A2 and PSEN1 (P-1232 p3, p4, p5 and p9 quotes).
The pack's performance-validity flag on P-1254 does not apply on the PDF: its highest AUC is 0.901 (P-1254 p1 quote).

We selected two genes (ATP2A2 and PSEN1) for analysis during this process.

challenge.by: second model reader instructed to argue the verdict into a genuine contradiction (or out of one), reading both source documents in full
challenge.strongest_case_against_the_verdict: Frame the quantity as the in-sample ROC AUC of a plasma-exosomal non-coding-RNA signature for MCI against community controls in Chinese elderly, measured by ultracentrifugation and qPCR. Task (T1), modality family (fluid, plasma exosomal RNA) and validation tier (both contested AUCs are in-sample) then match, the metric type is the same, and the one failing gate (dataset family: Guangzhou v Gansu community cohorts) is of the kind the review once waived (C-232, ADNI v NACC). Each study's uncertainty excludes the other's estimate: P-1232's 0.641-0.760 excludes 0.901, and a Hanley-McNeil interval for 0.901 with 24 v 24 (about 0.81-0.99, reader's calculation) excludes 0.700. Two ordering-type statements could be read as crossing the pair: P-1232 says its combination was 'more credible' than single markers and that exosomal lncRNAs 'may offer a broader research space and prospect ... compared to miRNAs', while a single exosomal miRNA in P-1254 beats the lncRNA panel by 0.20. A second shared quantity also seems to split: P-1254 finds education and regular exercise significantly associated with MCI and concludes that they 'help older people maintain cognitive function', whereas P-1232 finds no case-control difference in education or physical activity.
challenge.why_it_does_or_does_not_succeed: It does not succeed. (1) 'A plasma-exosomal ncRNA signature' is not one estimand: an AUC belongs to a specific predictor in a specific population, the rule names predictor set as a quantity difference, and it lists 'two different methods each reporting a different score where neither study claims the ordering the other refutes' as not incompatible. Neither paper measures the other's markers. In summaries.md, miR-483-5p, miR-502-5p and the three lncRNAs occur only in these two blocks, and the other exosomal-miRNA papers (e.g. P-1323) use different miRNAs, so there is no same-marker or bridging study. (2) The ordering-type statements stay inside one paper: 'more credible' compares the panel with its own three lncRNAs; the lncRNA-versus-miRNA sentence is hedged ('may'), concerns research scope, and is derived from 'a broader range of biological functions', not from accuracy data (P-1232 measured no miRNA); P-1254 never mentions lncRNAs. (3) Waiving the dataset family would not help: the C-232 cohort waiver was later judged insufficient because predictor-set and horizon differences remained, and here predictor set, case definition (education-specific MMSE v uncorrected MoCA < 26) and control group all differ. The control groups are age/sex-matched v 4.8 years younger, and P-1254 prints a MoCA SD of 1.14 around 26.17, which 24 integer scores all at or above 26 cannot produce. (4) The lifestyle quantities fail Section 5.2: education is same-direction (illiterate 10.3% v 7.1% of cases v controls in P-1232; 20/99 v 3/176 in P-1254) with a significance-only difference. The exercise contrast sets a null with no supported direction (88.4% v 87.1% regular, p = 0.729, age/sex-matched) against a crude association in a sample whose MCI cases average 78.17 v 71.21 years. Neither paper reports an interval, and the dataset-family gate fails for these quantities too. (5) The performance-validity flag is correctly not applied to P-1254 (AUC 0.901; accuracy 43/48 = 0.896 at the reported operating point), consistent with its application to P-988 (AUC 1.0) in C-236; applying it would only add a further bar to genuine. (6) I also tested the other direction, false_positive: the record uses the 'Both findings (can) stand' fork template that the first reader labelled false_positive in C-235 and C-236. There, the claimed opposition dissolved on reading (misread papers, same-direction results). Here a non-overlapping numeric gap survives and the record keeps open that it is an artefact, so the precise failure is the quantity (outcome 2). The first reader's verdict and grounds stand.
grounds: The two AUCs are for different predictors, a logistic combination of three exosomal lncRNAs in P-1232 and one literature-preselected exosomal miRNA in P-1254, and neither study measures the other's markers, so under the rule (predictor set) they are different quantities [e1, e10, e17].

The only ordering-type statements stay inside one paper: P-1232's 'more credible' compares its panel with its own three lncRNAs, and its lncRNA-versus-miRNA sentence is a hedged remark about research scope derived from breadth of biological function, not an accuracy result (P-1232 measured no miRNA), while P-1254 never mentions lncRNAs [e2, e3, e4].

The populations behind the shared 'MCI vs healthy controls' label differ: education-specific MMSE cut-offs with age/sex-matched controls against MoCA < 26 with controls 4.8 years younger than the cases, on two scales for which neither paper reports a common metric [e5, e6, e12, e16].

P-1254's age-matched controls cannot all be normal by its own MoCA >= 26 rule unless its table is misprinted, because 24 integer scores all at or above 26 with mean 26.17 allow a standard deviation of at most about 0.82, not the printed 1.14 (reader's arithmetic) [e12, e16].

The dataset-family gate fails with no waiver on record, and a waiver would not change the outcome: C-232's cohort waiver was itself judged insufficient once predictor-set differences were found, and the predictor sets differ here too.

The numeric gap is real in form (P-1232's interval 0.641-0.760 excludes 0.901; a Hanley-McNeil interval of about 0.81-0.99 for 0.901 with 24 v 24, reader's calculation, excludes 0.700), so the verdict rests on the quantity difference and not on noise [e1, e10].

The second quantity both papers report, lifestyle correlates of MCI, gives no contradiction under Section 5.2: education points the same way in both with a significance-only difference, and for exercise P-1232's age/sex-matched null (p = 0.729) has no direction of its own while P-1254's crude association (p = 0.017) comes from a sample whose cases are about 7 years older, with no interval reported by either [e7, e8, e11, e13, e14, e15].

The performance-validity flag correctly does not apply to P-1254 (highest AUC 0.901; implied accuracy 43/48 = 0.896), consistent with the first reader's use of the 0.97 threshold for P-988 (AUC 1.0, C-236), so it neither blocks nor supports genuine here [e10].

The architectural-fork alternative (false_positive) was tested because the record shares the 'Both findings (can) stand' template of C-235 and C-236, but here a non-overlapping numeric gap survives the reading and the record keeps open that it is artefact, so documented_incommensurability is the precise outcome; both labels exclude genuine.

unresolved_discrepancy_2026_09_30.summary: Two community studies using plasma exosomal RNA to separate Chinese older adults with MCI from controls report AUCs that differ beyond their combined uncertainty: P-1254 reports 0.901 for miR-483-5p, in-sample, in 24 v 24 people, and P-1232 reports 0.700 (95% CI 0.641-0.760) for a three-lncRNA panel in 150 v 150 (z = 3.62). The studies measure different markers, which is the leading candidate explanation; P-1254's in-sample estimate after marker selection, its younger controls, the MCI definitions and the cohorts are others, and none is shown to be sufficient.
candidate_explanations: Different analytes: a three-lncRNA logistic panel (P-1232) against single miRNAs (P-1254); each study measures only its own markers. This is the leading candidate.
Marker preselection and in-sample optimism in P-1254: four literature candidates, ROC reported only for the two that separated the groups, 48 people, no CI, cross-validation or external cohort.
Sample size: 24 v 24 against 150 v 150.
Control group: P-1254's 'age-matched' controls average 73.35 years against 78.12 for MCI, and 'CD9 showed an increasing trend dependent on age'; P-1232's controls are matched 1:1.
Label definition: education-specific MMSE cut-offs (P-1232) against MoCA < 26 plus European Consortium criteria (P-1254).
Cohort: Guangzhou community case-control sample against a Gansu community survey.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.

conflicts.claim_b: The apparent positive arm. N=105 pooled English three-source connected-speech sample (35 HC / 35 MCI / 35 AD), transcript-level referential grammar. conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY - NOT a genuine conflict, filed so the pair is not regenerated. P-747 and P-748 are the most collidable pair in the speech/language frontier: same publication year (2022), same journal (Journal of Neurolinguistics), same elicitation paradigm (picture description), same diagnostic groups (HC / amnestic MCI / AD), same task code T4, same cross-sectional design, same validation tier V2, and headline directions that read as opposite - P-747 reports that not one of fourteen gestural variables reached p below 0.05 and that gesture correlates with neither MMSE nor study group, while P-748 reports the adjunct clause ratio separating MCI from controls at Cohen's d .93. They are nevertheless incommensurable on three independent grounds. (1) CHANNEL: they measure different channels of the same elicitation task - manually annotated co-speech hand gesture versus transcribed referential grammar - so 'does picture description carry an MCI signal' is not one question they both answer. (2) NO METRIC: neither paper computes any discrimination statistic of any kind, so no gap magnitude exists and none can be constructed; any performance row sourced from either would be an artefact of P-747's title word 'discriminate'. (3) OVERCLAIM: P-747's card carries authors_overclaim and its three headline variables sit at p .088, .060 and .088 in cells of ten to eleven, so it cannot be the strong arm of anything. Where the two papers DO measure the same quantity - the type-token ratio - they AGREE: both report it null. The pair should be carried as convergent on generic surface measures and silent on each other elsewhere.

conflicts.claim_a: The unloaded arm and the apparent negative. Free viewing of 32 real-world photographs, 32 aMCI vs 32 HC, nine parameters, none separating aMCI from HC; no classifier and no ROC analysis of any kind, so it produces no discrimination figure that could be placed against an AUC. It also supplies, from its own literature review, the field's position that the documented aMCI oculomotor abnormalities are SACCADE-TASK abnormalities - which is what makes the paradigm reading a source-grounded reading rat
conflicts.claim_b: The loaded arm in an independent cohort (Korea Institute of Oriental Medicine / GARD, 79 MCI vs 170 age-matched HC). Inhibition errors and failure to self-correct in interleaved prosaccade/antisaccade and Go/No-go. Reports group differences only and no classification AUC, which is itself part of why the pairing with P-686 is not adjudicable as a conflict.
conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY, NOT A GENUINE CONFLICT. P-686's amnestic-MCI null (not one of nine eye-movement parameters separated aMCI from healthy controls) does not contradict the positive eye-movement MCI results in this frontier (P-966, P-1163); the apparent contradiction is a paradigm boundary and gatecheck refuses both pairings. The discriminating variable is attentional/executive LOAD, not eye tracking as a channel: the signal appears under inhibitory-control and divided-attention demand (P-966 interleaved prosaccade/antisaccade and Go/No-go, 79 MCI vs 170 HC; P-1163 peripheral Useful-Field-of-View reaction time) and is absent under passive or unloaded viewing (P-686 free viewing of real-world photographs; P-1163's own central visual-field task, null in the SAME 74 participants). P-1163 therefore replicates the boundary WITHIN one study, which is the strongest form of the evidence because participants, hardware and reference standard are held constant across the loaded and unloaded arms. The corpus record that should follow is a scope boundary on VF-18 ('Ocular channels ... are repeatedly supported as scalable biomarker directions', supporters include P-966): the eye-movement half of VF-18 is demonstrated only for load paradigms, and passive free viewing is a null channel. P-686 bounds that claim rather than refuting it, because its own null is reported without an effect size, without an interval and without an equivalence test, and the paper leaves underpowering at 32 per group open as an alternative explanation.

evidence_quotes.supports: The paradigm reading comes from P-686's own account of the field: what the literature documents in aMCI are saccade-task measures, which is exactly the class P-966 and P-1163 sample and the class P-686 did not use.

evidence_quotes.quote: It should be read as a negative result constraining that literature, not as a detection-performance record, and must not be entered as supporting evidence for any verified finding about eye-movement-based MCI detection.

conflicts.residual_risk: The load-versus-unloaded axis is a post-hoc reading imposed across three papers, none of which set out to test it, and it has a competing explanation that this evidence cannot exclude: stimulus complexity and free response. P-686's free viewing of 32 natural photographs has no correct answer and no reaction-time demand, whereas both positive paradigms are speeded forced-response tasks with an error that can be scored - so 'speeded scoreable response' may be the operative variable rather than 'attentional load', and P-1163's central-versus-peripheral dissociation is consistent with either since both its arms are speeded. Two further weaknesses. First, P-686's null has 32 aMCI participants and no power analysis, so the boundary's negative side rests on a result the paper itself will not call demonstrated absence. Second, the loaded side is thinner than three papers suggest: P-1006, the other load-positive paper in this pack, shares four authors (Opwonya, Lee, Kim, Kim) and the GARD cohort with P-966, and gatecheck cf P-966 P-1006 nonetheless prints PASS, so the non-independence registry does not currently see this pair - the effective count of independent load-positive cohorts here is two, not three.

Existing gaps G-02, G-10, G-15, G-CAND-42, ACTOR-G-002/006/060/068 are all about retinal STRUCTURE and ocular functional electrophysiology (OCT, OCTA, choroid, fundus ML, PVEP/FERG longitudinal validation); none concerns eye-movement paradigms. No conflict in conflicts.json involves P-686, P-966 or P-1163 (the conflict pool lists only P-247 x P-1006, P-247 x P-1163 and P-1006 x P-1163 for this theme). Distinct from sibling candidate T03_retina_eye-gap-03, which makes a REPORTING claim (positives carry effect sizes, negatives do not) about the same P-686 null; this record makes a SUBSTANTIVE claim about which oculomotor paradigms carry MCI signal, and its corroborating datum - the central-versus-peripheral dissociation inside P-1163 - appears in no existing record or candidate. Distinct from T03_retina_eye-gap-02, which is about the screener-defined reference standard, an axis this record does not use.

TASK_SUBSTAGE_MISMATCH: this is one of the reasons the record exists, not a defect in it - registry task_substage is 'visual_scanning' for P-686 against 'mci_vs_hc_saccade' (P-966) and 'MCI_vs_HC' (P-1163), and the record's claim is precisely that the substage difference is the finding.

DESIGN_MISMATCH: P-686 is case_control and Task_Type T4 (group comparison, no classifier); P-966 and P-1163 are cross_sectional T1. Stated, not overridden.
DUPLICATE_PAPER: cleared - gatecheck show prints duplicate_of 'not reported' for P-686 and '-' for P-966 and P-1163.

NON-INDEPENDENCE: cleared for the three papers used. P-686 is Dokuz Eylul University, Izmir (Eraslan Boz et al.); P-966 is the Korea Institute of Oriental Medicine / GARD cohort (Opwonya et al.); P-1163 is a Kyoto care-facility cohort (Tamaru et al.). AUTHORS_OVERCLAIM (schema rule 2): no strong arm is being claimed, since no conflict is being claimed. conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY, NOT A GENUINE CONFLICT. P-1153 and P-1154 both use baseline 18F-FDG-PET to predict future dementia in non-demented elderly and report prognostic ceilings roughly 0.2 AUC apart (P-1153: iAUC 0.768 -> 0.787, Delta 0.020, adding a deep-learning FDG score to clinical variables; P-1154: AUC 0.994 for direct normal-to-dementia conversion from a baseline FDG MetaROI z-score). The pair passes all four deterministic conflict gates and would therefore be generated as a genuine-conflict candidate, but it must NOT be promoted: the two papers differ in baseline population (baseline-MCI vs cognitively normal), in endpoint (incremental prediction of any cognitive decline vs standalone prediction of membership in a post-hoc-labelled bypass-MCI pathway) and in metric construction (incremental integrated time-dependent AUC over a clinical model vs absolute cross-validated classification AUC), and BOTH arms carry authors_overclaim flags, so the pair has no admissible strong arm. The usable output is a boundary condition: P-1154's 0.994 must not be ingested as an FDG-PET prognostic benchmark, and the externally validated arm (P-1153, V3, three cohorts) is what bounds FDG-PET's real incremental prognostic value at Delta iAUC 0.020-0.059.

conflicts.residual_risk: The strongest objection is that the explanation may be instrument rather than power. P-687 measures Timed Up and Go time, which bundles a sit-to-stand transfer and a 180-degree turn with walking, and P-1082 measures Kinect-derived macro markers over a 10 m path, whereas P-761 and P-695 measure steady-state spatiotemporal walkway parameters and usual-pace speed. A real possibility remains that TUG total time and Kinect macro velocity genuinely have poorer unloaded sensitivity than walkway step velocity for structural reasons - different measurement error, different ceiling - in which case the load-necessary claim would be instrument-conditional rather than simply under-powered, and this record would be right that the generalisation is unsafe but wrong about why. Nothing in these four papers can separate the two accounts, because no study in the pack measures both a walkway parameter and a loaded task in the same participants at a sample size adequate to test the interaction.

conflicts.conflict_statement: PRE-EMPTIVE INCOMMENSURABILITY RULING on a pair the pipeline will generate. P-709 and P-1013 both carry Task_Type T4, both are coded study_design_type cross_sectional, both are single-site MCI cohorts of comparable size, and both publish a fall-risk discrimination figure - AUC 0.825 for the Four Square Step Test (P-709) against accuracy 0.53-0.81, sensitivity 0.82-0.99, specificity 0.69-0.90 for a wearable postural-sway system (P-1013). They are therefore an attractive candidate pair, and any performance comparison drawn across them is invalid, because neither number measures the quantity its title names and the two mislabellings are different. P-709's positives are MCI patients who RECALL a fall in the preceding 12 months, ascertained by self-report in a cohort selected for memory impairment, so the label is misclassified by the deficit that defines the sample and the resulting 15.11 s cut-off is displaced by an unsigned amount. P-1013's positives are never falls at all: the wearable is scored against agreement with Berg Balance Scale and Timed Up and Go performance, and its comparison arm is 20 healthy adults of mean age 25.20 set against 20 MCI patients of mean age 79.00, a 54-year gap that leaves age as an unremoved explanation for whatever the device discriminates. LEDGER ACTIONS: (1) route P-709 x P-1013 to documented_incommensurability before any conflict pass, not to genuine; (2) bar P-709's AUC 0.825 from serving as the strong arm of any conflict and from supporting any verified finding phrased as fall PREDICTION, since its own appraisal states the analysis 'does not predict anything'; (3) bar P-1013's accuracy range from any MCI-versus-control performance comparison, since half its sample is not older adults. The corpus's only prospectively ascertained falls result (P-695, monthly fall calendars) is null in every stratum (PrC p = 0.185, MCI p = 0.232, AD p = 0.528) and is itself under-powered, so there is no third number that could adjudicate between them. COMPLEMENTS, does not restate, sibling candidate T06_gait_motor_wearable-gap-01, which states the research absence (no fall-risk operating point in MCI is calibrated against an observed fall); this record states the ledger consequence for a specific pair.

record_defects: Two sentences are filed under paper P-709, and the conflict_statement calls the first 'its own appraisal': 'it does not predict anything' and 'in a cohort selected for memory impairment the outcome measure is contaminated by the very deficit that defines the exposure group'. Neither is in the P-709 PDF; both are summary-block appraisal. The PDF's own caveat is recall bias 'underestimating fall frequency' (p. 6), and its authors present the cut-off as marking high fall risk (p. 5). The underlying facts are correct: 12-month self-report recorded at baseline, and a cut-off derived and evaluated in the same 46 participants.

'P-1013's positives are never falls at all' is too strong. Section 2.5 defines positives for the cut-off analysis as participants 'who experienced falls within 3 months'; only Section 2.4 names BBS < 40 / TUG > 14 s as the ROC criterion. The paper is internally inconsistent. In the Section 2.5 reading the positive class coincides with the MCI group, because a fall in the past 3 months was an MCI inclusion criterion.

The record sets P-709's AUC against P-1013's accuracy, sensitivity and specificity, and the gate output warns of an AUC_ROC vs Accuracy metric mismatch. But P-1013 reports ROC AUCs of 0.82-0.94 with 95% CIs (Table 2), so metric type is not what separates the pair.

'both are single-site MCI cohorts of comparable size': half of P-1013's sample (20 of 40) is healthy adults aged about 25, and its MCI group is defined by MMSE 20-23, ABC score and a recent fall, not by a clinical diagnosis. P-709 uses neurologist-assigned CDR 0.5, and the ROC samples are 46 vs 40.

'null in every stratum' for P-695 is correct for any fall, but P-695's Table 4 reports recurrent falls in MCI at p = 0.017 (interval 5.582-30969485). The record's per-group p-values follow P-695's Table 3, which P-695's own text contradicts.

conflicts.claim_a: The positive arm, and the reason no genuine conflict can be built: it is the only paper claiming benefit on executive-function subdomains, it carries authors_overclaim, and its own pooled estimates double-count at least two underlying trials. It also supplies the overlap evidence against P-839 (a dance-based trial coded as aerobic exercise inside its own Table 1).
conflicts.claim_b: One of the two null arms. VR-wrapped combined cognitive-plus-physical training, 7 RCTs / 188 participants. Its null on memory and executive function/attention is stated by the authors inside their own limitations section, alongside the concession that the evidence base is too small to settle the question.
conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY - do not promote as a genuine conflict. Three MCI intervention meta-analyses in this pack report opposite directions on the same outcome family (executive function / attention in older adults with MCI): P-834 concludes that exercise produced positive benefits across multiple executive-function subdomains (24 RCTs, 2278 participants; delayed-recall pool MD 0.61, 95 per cent CI 0.33-0.90), while P-833 concedes an explicit null for memory and executive function/attention (7 RCTs, 188 participants) and P-839 states an explicit null for executive function (8 pooled RCTs, 600 MCI participants). The deterministic gate PASSES all three pairings, because in the T6|review_meta cell both task_substage and modality_subtype are 'not reported' on every side, so the two gates that exist to catch exactly this are skipped rather than applied - the cell is currently gate-vacuous and will keep minting candidates of this shape. The three results are nevertheless incommensurable for four independent reasons: (1) the intervention families differ (structured exercise / VR-wrapped combined cognitive-physical training / dance movement), which is the MODALITY_SUBTYPE_MISMATCH pattern the operator split out of C-229 for digital cognitive training; (2) the two nulls rest on pools an order of magnitude smaller than the positive and are conceded by their own authors as thin, so they are failures to detect, not contrary estimates; (3) the pools plausibly share primary trials - P-834's own Table 1 includes a dance-based exercise trial coded as aerobic exercise, so its intervention class overlaps P-839's whole subject matter, and P-839's per-study list does not survive extraction, making the overlap unverifiable rather than absent; (4) P-834, the only positive arm and therefore the only possible strong arm, both carries an authors_overclaim flag and double-counts at least two underlying trials across multiple reports, violating the independence assumption its own inverse-variance pooling rests on. The useful record here is the gate defect plus the incommensurability, not a disagreement.

Its data-driven statistical method (LCA) classifies FEWER participants as MCI than consensus (41% vs 44%), and its conclusion favours consensus for prognosis. It is the arm whose numbers are explicit and per-method.
conflicts.claim_b: Arm B. agnes hierarchical clustering of the NACC UDS neuropsychological battery in 26,255 non-demented participants, reporting that clustering identified MORE MCI than consensus and framing this as outperforming consensus diagnosis. It is the arm that supplies the direction claim - but it supplies NO count for it, which is itself part of why the pair cannot be adjudicated.
conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY - NOT a genuine conflict. P-955 (Penn Memory Center / ADRC, N=354) and P-1084 (NACC Uniform Data Set, N=26,255) both score a data-driven classification of the neuropsychological battery against clinical consensus MCI diagnosis, in US Alzheimer's Disease Research Center participants, on battery scores alone, and report OPPOSITE directions for the same quantity: P-955's latent class analysis labels FEWER people MCI than consensus (41% LCA vs 44% consensus vs 53% actuarial Jak/Bondi) while P-1084's agnes cluster analysis 'identified more MCI cases than consensus diagnosis' and is titled and framed as showing data-driven subtyping 'outperforms consensus diagnosis in identifying MCI cases'. The pair must NOT be promoted as a conflict, for four independent reasons: (1) gatecheck fails five gates (Task_Type T6 vs T2, design, task_substage, population_specificity, metric type); (2) the sampling frames differ in consensus-MCI base rate - P-955's memory-clinic ADRC sample is already 44% consensus-MCI, while 16,005 of P-1084's 26,255 non-demented participants carry a consensus 'normal cognition' label - so the direction in which a data-driven partition departs from consensus is a function of the frame, not of the method; (3) neither study has a reference standard independent of the consensus label it is scoring against (P-955: 'no biomarker confirmation'; P-1084: 'survival endpoints rely on clinical diagnosis'), so neither 'more' nor 'fewer' can be read as more or fewer TRUE cases; (4) Penn's ADRC is one of the NIA ADRCs that contribute to the NACC UDS, so P-955's 354 participants are structurally inside P-1084's 26,255 rather than an independent sample. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE KB: 'data-driven neuropsychological subtyping identifies more MCI than consensus diagnosis' is not an established direction in this corpus and must not be recorded as one - P-1084's registry Best_Metric currently carries the string 'MCI cases beyond consensus diagnosis' in the position of a measured metric, and P-1084's card already flags that claim as authors_overclaim.

conflicts.claim_a: Arm A. Population-based Swedish cohort applying Petersen and a modified NP rule to the same 5,804 examined participants and reporting reversion under each; concludes stability does not distinguish the two rules and that reversion is not an artefact of the laxer definition.
conflicts.claim_b: Arm B. Population-based Italian cohort applying Petersen/Winblad and Jak/Bondi to the same 1,021 participants over 12 years and reporting a 20-point diagnostic-consistency advantage for the neuropsychological rule, alongside comparable dementia risk under both.
conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY, NOT PROPOSED AS GENUINE. The corpus contains two population-cohort studies that apply BOTH dominant MCI operationalisations (Petersen/Winblad conventional vs Jak/Bondi-style neuropsychological) to the same participants and report OPPOSITE orderings on the same practical question - which rule yields the more stable MCI diagnosis. P-986 (Swedish GAS/SNAC, n=744 Petersen and n=375 NP, median ~7 years) finds reversion 43.4% (95% CI 39.8-47.0) under Petersen versus 48.3% (43.2-53.5) under NP and concludes neither definition is superior on stability; P-1136 (Italian InveCe.Ab, n=1,021, 12 years) finds neuropsychological criteria produce more consistent diagnoses, 63.2% versus 43.2%. The two results cannot be adjudicated against each other because they are not the same measurement: P-986 measures a single MCI-to-non-MCI reversion transition over ~7 years with confidence intervals, P-1136 measures whole-period diagnostic consistency over 12 years with no test statistic, and the two NP arms are not the same rule (P-986 retains a subjective-complaint requirement that the original Jak criteria do not). The record's value is the closure test it names, not a winner.

conflicts.residual_risk: The disagreement may be entirely manufactured by the estimand difference and therefore not worth a record at all. Diagnostic consistency over 12 years and reversion at a follow-up wave over ~7 years are different functions of the same underlying trajectories, and it is arithmetically possible for the neuropsychological rule to produce both more reversion transitions (P-986) and more whole-period label consistency (P-1136) without either result being wrong - for instance if NP reverters revert once and stay reverted while conventional-criteria cases oscillate. If that is what is happening, the honest record is a measurement-definition note, not a disagreement, and the two papers agree that criteria choice matters while differing only in which axis of stability they chose to report. A second, weaker objection: P-1136's consistency figure carries no confidence interval and no between-criteria test, so its 20-point gap may not be distinguishable from P-986's overlapping-CI null in the first place.

Same-participant frame differs (P-986 n = 334 with data for both criteria; P-1136 280 with MCI under both).

Norms: external SNAC norms against internal InveCe.Ab norms.

conflicts.claim_b: The closest claim-level counterpart and the reason this record exists: a narrative review whose central thesis is multimodal synergy in MCI, built with no pooled estimates. This is the paper whose conclusion P-895 most directly tests, because P-895's CPR arm is precisely a cognitive + physical + risk-factor multimodal package in MCI.
conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY, NOT A GENUINE CONFLICT. The corpus's multi-domain non-pharmacological position for MCI - that combining cognitive, physical and lifestyle components improves cognition - is asserted by three syntheses in this slice (P-914, P-1077, P-1131) none of which reports a single pooled effect size, and is contradicted at the claim level by P-895, an MCI-only, preregistered, 456-participant, blinded-endpoint, Bonferroni-corrected primary-care RCT of exactly that intervention shape (cognitive training + Tai Chi + nurse-led risk-factor modification versus health advice), which is flatly null on its pre-specified ADAS-Cog primary endpoint at 15 months and at 6 and 12 months. This must NOT be promoted to a genuine conflict: gatecheck refuses all three pairings on study_design_type (rct versus review), and no gap magnitude is computable in any of them because the review side reports no effect size of any kind. What survives as a usable record is the EVIDENTIAL ASYMMETRY and its mechanism. P-914's multimodal-synergy thesis is narrative with no pooled estimate; P-1131 concludes combined exercise is superior while conceding 'none used meta-analytic pooling of effect sizes'; and P-1077's positive verdict is a vote count in which a trial is scored positive if it is significant on AT LEAST ONE domain, a rule the review itself flags as 'reliance on significance voting (19/20) rather than effect magnitude'. P-895 pre-specified ONE endpoint and corrected for multiplicity, and it is null - and it records that all three arms, including the booklet-only control, improved within-group. P-895 postdates the search windows of P-1077 (to 2023) and P-1131 (Feb 2023) and is named by none of the three, so it is independent of all of them and is not double-counted inside any. CONSEQUENCE: no verified finding, Table 6.5 row or synthesis sentence asserting multi-domain / combined non-pharmacological efficacy in MCI should cite P-914, P-1077 or P-1131 without carrying P-895 as the countervailing trial-level estimate, and the corpus currently holds P-895 in no gap and in only one CF pair.

Revised 2026-09-14: that stratification is NOT a bound on the definitional family - it accounts for only 30 of the 48 pooled studies, and two of the remainder, including the largest at n = 7422 (Sha 2022, roughly 23 per cent of the pooled sample), ascertain MCI from MMSE alone.
conflicts.claim_b: The low outlier and the paper that supplies its own explanation. Frontier community cohort (CLHLS 2008-2018, N=11,211) reporting 9.4 per cent MCI-to-NC reversion under an MCI definition of CMMSE below 18; its digest states the rate is not comparable with the wider literature and leaves open whether 9.4 per cent is a property of the population or of the threshold.
conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY - EXPLICITLY NOT PROPOSED AS A GENUINE CONFLICT (gatecheck prints FAIL on four gates: Task_Type T5 vs T6, study_design_type longitudinal_2point vs review_meta_analysis, population_specificity general vs MCI, modality_subtype population_cohort_epidemiology vs meta_analysis_pooled; task_substage PASSES at MCI_reversion and the metric-type difference is a WARN, not a gate failure). P-722 (CLHLS, 11,211 community-dwelling Chinese adults aged 65+, mean age 85.80 years, continuous-time multi-state Markov model) reports MCI-to-normal-cognition reversion at 9.4 per cent against the 36 per cent P-711 pools for community-based studies. The two figures are not two estimates of one quantity, and the record rests on two grounds that survive re-reading. FIRST, the estimands differ in kind: P-711 pools study-level observed proportions of reverters across 48 studies and 31,876 subjects, whereas P-722's 9.4 per cent is a modelled transition probability from a continuous-time multi-state Markov model in which death is an explicit absorbing state rather than censoring. SECOND, and decisive for the denominator, 75 per cent of P-722's baseline-MCI transitions go to death (14 per cent remain MCI, 9 per cent revert, 1 per cent progress to dementia), so its reversion share is arithmetically compressed relative to any pooled proportion of observed reverters in younger, surviving samples. A third, descriptive difference is that P-722's 'MCI' is a single global-screen threshold (CMMSE below 18 with absence of dementia, no neuropsychological domain profiling) rather than a criterion-based diagnosis, and P-722's own appraisal states that on this definition 'the reversion rate is not comparable with the wider literature'. WITHDRAWN AT OPERATOR REVIEW 2026-09-14: this record previously asserted, as its decisive quantitative point, that the 9.4-versus-28-to-36 per cent gap exceeds the criterion-level heterogeneity P-711 measures and therefore places P-722's operationalisation OUTSIDE the family of definitions VF-33 rests on, and on that basis asked for a VF-33 scope condition restricting the 30-48 per cent band to multi-domain / criterion-based MCI ascertainment. Both clauses are withdrawn. P-711's criterion stratification accounts for only 30 of its 48 pooled studies, and two of the remainder - including its largest contributor, Sha 2022 at n = 7422, roughly 23 per cent of the pooled sample - ascertain MCI from MMSE alone, a screening instrument of P-722's own kind. The between-criterion spread of pooled means is therefore not a bound on the definitional family, and the proposed scope condition would have excluded P-711's own largest contributor. Ledger consequence (retained): P-722 must not be admitted as a supporter of VF-33 and must not be recorded as refuting it; P-722 is already listed in VF-33's rejected_supporters, so that bookkeeping is already realised. No scope condition is written onto VF-33 on this record's reasoning.

conflicts.conflict_statement: FILED AS A DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY, NOT AS A GENUINE CONFLICT (the pair prints FAIL on the conflict gate; see gatecheck_output). The corpus holds two population-level statements about how much dementia is actually diagnosed in high-income settings that are numerically incompatible at face value: P-1046 reports US Medicare dementia detection at 1.086-1.104 of expected across 2015-2019 - i.e. dementia is detected at or slightly above the expected rate - while P-977 reports that only 40-50 percent of people with dementia in high-income countries have received a diagnosis. The discrepancy is not a disagreement about how many diagnoses were made; it is created entirely by the DENOMINATOR convention. P-1046's 'expected' is a probit model fitted on HRS 2000-2016 and transported onto Medicare claims; P-977's denominator is epidemiologically estimated dementia prevalence in national populations. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE KB: neither number may be cited as 'the' dementia detection rate, the two may never be pooled or differenced, and P-1046's headline figure that about 92 percent of expected MCI is undiagnosed inherits exactly the same denominator dependence - it is a statement about the HRS-transported expectation as much as about clinical practice, and it must be quoted with that qualifier attached.

That null is well powered, not a coverage artefact: the late-life stratum is 1,543 participants sleeping 7 hours or more (mean 7.68 +/- 0.82 h) carrying 245 aMCI cases (summaries.md L77642, L77654). The contrast with P-891 is therefore dissolved by outcome definition, estimand and age window, not by P-773 being underpowered.
conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY - explicitly NOT a genuine conflict, and filed so that this pair is not minted as one. P-891 (CHARLS 2018, n = 7,480, Chinese adults 45+) and P-773 (CLAS 2011-12, n = 2,977, Chinese adults 60-96) pass every deterministic comparability gate - same Task_Type T6, same design cross_sectional, same population class 'general', same modality_subtype survey_questionnaire, same validation tier V2, independent cohorts - and they appear to disagree about the LONG-SLEEP arm of the sleep-MCI dose-response: P-891 reports elevated MCI odds among long sleepers (OR 1.88 with poor sleep quality against 1.33 with good sleep quality), while P-773 reports no association above the 7-hour cut (OR 0.91, 0.77-1.08, p = 0.283 per additional hour). The pair must NOT be recorded as a conflict for three reasons that only the source text shows: (1) P-773's own curve estimation recovers the SAME inverted-U shape, with a late-life optimum of 6.87 hours, so the two papers agree on the shape and differ only on whether the right limb reaches significance; (2) P-773's null is NOT a coverage artefact and must not be described as one: its two long-sleep concessions belong to the YOUTH and MIDLIFE strata (137 participants above the 10-hour youth cut and 161 above the 9-hour midlife cut, one degenerate OR 0.00 estimate and one very wide interval - summaries.md L77690, L77642), whereas the late-life stratum on which the apparent disagreement sits holds 1,543 participants sleeping 7 hours or more (mean 7.68 +/- 0.82 h) with 245 aMCI cases (L77642, L77654), i.e. a well-powered null; (3) the two estimands are different contrasts - a per-additional-hour slope inside a >=7 h stratum against a >=8 h category contrast referenced to 6-8 h, and P-891's long-sleep odds ratios are sleep-quality-stratified with no unstratified main effect printed anywhere in its block - re-checked 2026-09-14: the block's only unstratified statement is qualitative ('Short (<=6 h) and long (>=8 h) sleep durations ... were linked to higher odds of MCI', L136092) and prints no OR and no confidence interval, so no interval comparison between the two papers is possible in either direction. The ruling therefore rests on outcome definition (TICS-10 screening MCI from age 45 vs Petersen amnestic MCI 60-96), estimand (per-additional-hour slope within a >=7 h stratum vs a quality-stratified >=8 h category contrast) and age window. Independently, neither paper is eligible to be the strong arm of any conflict: P-773 carries an authors_overclaim flag (interventional language on a cross-section) and P-891 carries a partial one (cross-sectional estimates converted into prescriptive sleep targets).

conflicts.claim_a: The quantified null arm, scoped to the SCD stage: a random-effects meta-analysis whose within-SCD comparator (SCD with affective symptoms against SCD without) yields a homogeneous null for depression on the MCI outcome (RR 0.98, 0.75-1.26, I2 = 0%) and on all outcomes combined (RR 0.90, 0.62-1.30), while its only positive pool is anxiety/SCD-related worry (RR 1.40, 1.20-1.63).
conflicts.claim_b: The unquantified positive arm, scoped to the MCI stage: a qualitative systematic review of 17 MCI-baseline longitudinal studies plus rodent work that names depression the strongest supported psychiatric risk factor for MCI-to-AD progression, with no pooled odds ratio, hazard ratio or risk ratio anywhere. It also supplies the field-position statement that makes the apparent contradiction legible.
conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY - explicitly NOT a genuine conflict, filed because the deterministic gates PASS this pair and a miner would otherwise mint it. P-831 (meta-analysis, 12 studies, 9 pooled for depression) and P-912 (systematic review, 17 longitudinal studies plus rodent literature) read as a head-on disagreement about whether depressive symptoms predict clinical progression: P-831 pools a tight, homogeneous NULL - 'Depression, MCI outcome | 4 (df 3) | 0.98 (0.75-1.26) | chi2 = 3.27, p = 0.35, I2 = 0%' with the authors' own verdict 'did not significantly increase the risk of MCI' - while P-912 'Consolidates depression as the strongest supported psychiatric risk factor for MCI-to-AD progression'. They are NOT in conflict, because the baseline clinical stage differs: P-831 measures progression among people who already have subjective cognitive decline (SCD -> MCI or dementia), P-912 measures progression among people who already have MCI (MCI -> AD). The gate cannot see this - the registry codes P-831's task_substage as 'not reported' and P-912's as 'risk_factor_synthesis' - and the two are additionally non-comparable in kind, since P-912 pools nothing and reports no effect estimate of any sort. The usable content is a STAGE BOUNDARY on the corpus's own verified position: VF-26 (depression and MCI robustly and reciprocally associated, with P-912 among its supporters) is not observed one stage earlier, where the pooled within-SCD depression estimate is null with I2 = 0%.

conflicts.claim_a: The null arm: a large single-centre memory-clinic study whose head-to-head of participant against informant report on one twelve-item instrument yields no participant-side relation to measured cognition in the whole population or in any stratum, with the authors stating the null is stronger than the prior literature.
conflicts.claim_b: The positive arm, in a disease-specific population and on a different estimand: a three-group PD study reporting moderate unadjusted correlations between complaints and objective memory and executive scores, concluding complaints have diagnostic validity in PD-MCI while conceding about a quarter of PD-MCI patients report no complaints at all.
conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY - explicitly NOT a genuine conflict; gatecheck returns FAIL and the pair is filed so the corpus does not over-generalise its strongest self-report null. Two papers in the same pack reach opposite verdicts on whether self-reported subjective cognitive complaints track measured cognition. P-862 (Taiwanese tertiary memory clinic, n = 1,536 across five diagnostic stages) reports a precise null: participant total complaints have no relation to the cognitive z-score in the whole population (B = -0.001, 95% CI -0.217 to 0.215, p = 0.993) and none in any diagnostic stratum, against B = -0.777 (p < 0.001) for informant report. P-883 (Brazilian movement-disorders clinic, n = 110) reports the opposite: complaints correlate with objective memory and executive scores (r = 0.38 to 0.52, p < 0.01) and the paper concludes complaints have diagnostic validity in PD-MCI. The pair fails the deterministic gate on population_specificity (general against PD_specific) and warns on metric type, and the two numbers are not estimates of the same quantity: an adjusted multivariable regression coefficient computed within and across five clinical strata against an unadjusted Pearson correlation over three diagnostically separated groups (PD-MCI, PD-NC, healthy controls) in which group separation alone will generate a moderate correlation. The usable content is a SCOPE BOUNDARY: the corpus's self-report null (P-862, and IA-10's confirmed prior that self-report is not as informative as informant report) must not be read as 'complaints carry no signal anywhere' - in PD-MCI, on an unadjusted between-group design, they do - and, symmetrically, P-883's 'valid clinical marker' conclusion cannot be imported into general memory-clinic populations.

conflicts.residual_risk: The strongest argument against this record is that the two papers may genuinely disagree about the same thing and I am dissolving it with a design story. P-862's whole-population participant estimate is the closest analogue of P-883's pooled correlation - both are computed across diagnostically mixed samples - and P-862's interval (-0.217 to 0.215) in a sample fourteen times larger excludes anything near r = 0.38, so the population and adjustment differences could be a post-hoc rescue rather than the explanation. Read against the extract, every quantity this record takes from P-883 is absent from it: (a) sample - 'We included 29 PD patients without MCI (PD-nMCI) and 11 PD patients with MCI (PD-MCI)' (L171-172) and '40 patients were included' (L342), not n=110, and there is NO healthy-control group, so the three-group design and the between-group-separation mechanism this record relies on do not exist; (b) estimand - the correlations are complaint dimension against health-related quality of life, not against objective tests: 'Non-parametric partial correlations between the Cognition and Communication dimensions, and the adjusted PDQ-39 SI were conducted' (L42-47), 'Spearman partial correlations were adjusted for UPDRS-III' (L439), Table 3 reporting Cognition PD-MCI rho .728 (p .017, FDR .034) and Communication PD-MCI rho .76 (p .011, FDR .043) against the adjusted PDQ-39 Summary Index (L423-437); r = 0.38-0.52 against memory/executive tests appears nowhere; (c) anosognosia - 'we evaluated anosognosia especially in the PD-MCI group through the clinical examination but none of the patients presented this symptom' (L208-213), the exact opposite of the 'approximately 24% of PD-MCI patients did not report significant cognitive complaints' quote this record uses; no Memory Complaint Scale, no BDI, no Apathy Scale, no ANCOVA and no Brazilian site occur in the extract. conflicts.claim_a: Strong arm on evidential weight, and the only corpus record that estimates a cholinergic-exposure effect on MCI-to-AD progression inside a single amyloid-characterised cohort with propensity weighting. Supplies the adverse-direction estimate (HR 1.77) and the Abeta-stratified subgroup estimate (HR 2.18). NOT usable as a causal arm: its own authors decline causal inference and name indication bias unresolved.
conflicts.claim_b: Weak arm. Supplies the field-facing preventive claim for a cholinergic precursor and is the reason this needs a record at all - it is the corpus text a reader would cite for 'cholinergic therapy prevents conversion in MCI'. Carries authors_overclaim, sponsor-funded medical writing, a post-publication correction, and no primary data, so it may not be used to offset or dilute P-1216.
conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY - NOT proposable as a genuine conflict. P-1216 (ADNI, 558 amnestic MCI, IPTW-weighted time-varying Cox, up to 10-year follow-up) finds cholinesterase-inhibitor exposure associated with HIGHER progression to AD dementia (HR 1.77, 95% CI 1.15-2.73) and much lower reversion to normal cognition (HR 0.17), with the highest risk in the Abeta+ stratum (HR 2.18); its own authors state that the observational design precludes causal conclusions and leave confounding by indication unresolved. P-1215 (narrative review) positions the cholinergic precursor choline alphoscerate as preventive therapy against AD in MCI, citing 8.2% vs 26.1% conversion over 3 years and recommending its addition to donepezil. The pair FAILS three comparability gates (Task_Type T2 vs T5; study_design_type survival_analysis vs review_meta_analysis; modality_subtype PET vs review_no_primary_data), SKIPS task_substage (not reported on one side), PASSES population_specificity, and carries a METRIC_TYPE_MISMATCH warning (Hazard_Ratio vs descriptive conversion percentages) which is a WARN and not a gate failure. The two drugs are different agent classes (ChEI vs precursor). REVISED AT OPERATOR REVIEW 2026-09-14, non-causal framing: this record does NOT assert that the two papers disagree. P-1216's unresolved confounding by indication means its HR 1.77 may be estimating the reason a drug was prescribed rather than an effect of the drug, so P-1216 does not show harm; and P-1215's preventive claim is not tested by it. OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE for the review paper and any synthesis built on this corpus, stated non-causally: the corpus may NOT be reported as showing that cholinergic drugs delay MCI-to-AD conversion, and it may NOT be reported as showing that they accelerate it. ALSO REVISED 2026-09-14: P-1216 is not the only corpus record on cholinergic exposure in MCI. P-929 (Seoul National University Bundang Hospital, 111 MCI at CDR 0.5, 73 ChEI users vs 38 non-users, amyloid PET within 6 months of baseline, propensity-matched subsample of 50) is a second, non-ADNI, amyloid-characterised record, and it is NULL rather than adverse: ChEI use was not associated with progression to CDR 1 at one year (OR 1.120, 95% CI 0.204-6.238, p = 0.892), with low baseline MMSE the only significant predictor. P-929 is weaker than P-1216 in horizon (1 year vs up to 10 years) and in endpoint (CDR-1 progression vs adjudicated AD dementia) and is itself retrospective with confounding by indication, so it does not refute P-1216; what it does is remove the 'only strong-design record' premise and leave the corpus with no replicated directional finding in either direction. P-1215 remains sponsor-funded, correction-issued, overclaim-flagged and resting on a single unreplicated Russian trial, so it may not be used to offset P-1216. The records must be reported side by side with their asymmetry stated, never pooled and never averaged.

record_defects: The conflict_statement says the claim rests 'on a single unreplicated Russian trial', and an evidence quote filed under P-1215 reads 'single study in Russia reported conversion benefits without independent replication'. In fact P-1215 cites a second source for reduced conversion, Kim et al. 2025, a nationwide longitudinal study in South Korea (p. 6). The quoted sentence is summary-block text, not in the PDF.

'recommending its addition to donepezil': P-1215's expert-opinion section (p. 8) recommends choline alphoscerate for cognitive disorders, affective alterations and pseudodepression, and gives dosing. It does not recommend the donepezil combination; it only reports that combination studies showed benefit (e.g. 'addition of choline alphoscerate to donepezil reduces brain atrophy in patients with MCI or Alzheimer’s disease', p. 7).

claim_a says 'its own authors decline causal inference'. The limitations do so ('allowing only for the assessment of associations', p. 10), but the abstract states 'Both ChEI use and Aβ burden independently accelerated MCI progression and cognitive decline' (p. 1, line-break hyphen removed), and the discussion attributes a mechanism to ChEIs. The authors use causal wording in the headline and hedge only in the limitations.

claim_a calls P-1216 'the only corpus record that estimates a cholinergic-exposure effect on MCI-to-AD progression inside a single amyloid-characterised cohort with propensity weighting'. P-929 (amyloid-PET-characterised, propensity-score matched) supersedes this, as the record's own revised conflict_statement concedes, but claim_a was never revised.

The record describes P-929 as using 'amyloid PET within 6 months of baseline'. The PDF also admitted positive scans taken more than 6 months before and negative scans taken more than 6 months after, and 27 of the 50 analysed participants had PET outside the 6-month window (p. 2).

Gate output 'FAIL Task_Type: T2 vs T5' and 'skip task_substage: not reported on one side' do not match the current registry row for P-1215, which reads Task_Type T6 and task_substage 'treatment_review'. This concerns registry state, not a PDF contradiction.

conflicts.claim_a: The large-sample class-level estimate. 128,683 hypertensive MCI patients, exposure defined at the level of five antihypertensive classes against non-use, class-level adjusted HRs 0.96-0.98 and no superior class. Not flagged for authors_overclaim - its own significance statement declines efficacy. Anchors the magnitude that a class-level claim has to answer to.
conflicts.claim_b: The small-sample count-level estimate whose class attribution is the incommensurable part. Exposure is a >=5-prescription polypharmacy band, not a drug class; the class sentence is a subgroup reading its own card flags as unsupported by any between-model test. Used here strictly as the weak arm and never as evidence of a class effect.
conflicts.conflict_statement: DOCUMENTED INCOMMENSURABILITY, NOT A GENUINE CONFLICT. The corpus's two estimates of a cardio-metabolic-medication effect on MCI-to-dementia progression sit an order of magnitude apart in the same direction and must not be pooled, ranked or read as replicating each other. P-999 (128,683 hypertensive patients with MCI, US Optum claims, Cox) puts each antihypertensive class at adjusted HR 0.96-0.98 versus non-use - a 2-4 per cent relative difference, essentially at the null - and finds no superior class on monotherapy comparison. P-1157 (237 Taiwanese MCI patients, Cox) reports adjusted HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.31-0.78) for a >=5-medication polypharmacy band and attributes it to antihypertensive and lipid-modifying agents. gatecheck FAILs the pair on population_specificity and modality_subtype, and behind that gate the two contrasts are different quantities: class-versus-nonuse inside an all-hypertensive MCI cohort, against a medication-COUNT band in a general veterans MCI cohort, with P-1157's class attribution a subgroup reading carrying no between-class test. The concrete hazard this record guards is already present in the corpus: P-1157's registry Key Novelty fuses the count-level hazard ratio with the class-level attribution in a single sentence, so any downstream synthesis that quotes 'HR 0.49' as the size of a cardio-metabolic drug-class effect is quoting a count contrast as if it were a class contrast, against a corpus estimate 600 times larger in sample that puts the class effect at the null.

readjudication_2026_09_27.quantity_a: Adjusted Cox HR for incident claims-coded ADRD after the first MCI diagnosis, for users of one antihypertensive class vs non-users of that class (who may use other classes), or any AHM vs none, in a cohort restricted to hypertensive patients (US Optum claims). Exposure is consumption 'during the study period', and the model is adjusted for statin and metformin use.
readjudication_2026_09_27.quantity_b: Adjusted Cox HR for neurologist-confirmed progression from CDR 0.5 to CDR 1, for baseline polypharmacy (5 or more prescription drugs vs fewer) and, secondarily, for baseline exposure to a drug category (e.g. any antihypertensive agent) vs no exposure. The cohort is general MCI veterans in Taiwan, about 65% hypertensive; the covariates include no hypertension term and no other medications.
grounds: On the record's own framing the exposures differ. P-999 contrasts users of one antihypertensive class with non-users of that class; P-1157's headline contrasts a medication count (5 or more prescription drugs) with fewer.

The closest like-for-like figures, which the record omits, are P-1157's antihypertensive-agent HR 0.59 and P-999's any-AHM-vs-none aHR 1.06. They point opposite ways, but the population behind the comparison differs. P-999 is restricted to hypertensive patients, so its comparator is untreated hypertensives. P-1157 includes MCI patients without hypertension, has no hypertension covariate, and finds hypertension itself more common among those who did not progress, so its estimate cannot be separated from hypertension status.

P-999 shows how far the estimate depends on the comparator and on co-medication: 0.96-0.98 per class against non-users of that class, 1.06 for any AHM against none, 0.84 with statins and 1.11 without. P-1157's per-category models adjust for no other medication, and its exposure is a baseline prescription, whereas P-999 counts consumption 'during the study period'.
The dataset-family gate fails, with no waiver on record.
No pairing of estimates across the two papers therefore estimates the same quantity, and the numerical gaps cannot be read as a contradiction.

evidence_quotes.quote: Users of each major AHM class showed significantly lower risk of developing ADRD compared to non-users of that specific drug class (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR): 0.96-0.98; all P≤0.048).
‘ARB non-users’ refer to patients that do not take any ARBs, but may or may not consume AHMs from other drug classes.
Patients who use any form of AHMs had 6% higher adjusted hazard ratio of ADRD (95% CI: (1.04, 1.08), P < 0.001) than non-users (Table 3).
the study population was narrowed down from patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) to hypertensive patients with MCI.

Under consumption of Statins, use of any AHMs or major AHM classes except for ‘Other’ AHMs showed protective effect against ADRD risk, whereas the use showed harmful effect under non-consumption of Statins.
The study included 100,678 patients who were taking at least one class of AHM and 28,005 who were not taking any AHMs during the study period.

Cox regression analysis revealed that polypharmacy was significantly associated with a reduced risk of MCI progression to dementia (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.31 to 0.78) after adjusting for covariates.

We observed that certain medications, such as antihypertensive agents (HR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.37 to 0.93) and lipid-modifying agents (HR = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.23 to 0.79), were significantly associated with a reduced risk of dementia progression.

record_defects: The conflict_statement says P-999 'puts each antihypertensive class at adjusted HR 0.96-0.98 versus non-use', and claim_a says 'five antihypertensive classes against non-use'. P-999's comparator is non-users of that specific class, who 'may or may not consume AHMs from other drug classes'. Against non-use of any AHM the estimate is aHR 1.06 (1.04-1.08), above 1 (Table 3).

'essentially at the null' / 'puts the class effect at the null': the class-level intervals exclude 1 for diuretics and CCBs (0.95-0.98) and reach 1.00 for the others. The authors report 'significantly lower risk' (all P <= 0.048) and conclude that 'All five major AHM classes showed a protective effect'. The effects are small, but the paper does not report them as null.

'P-1157's class attribution a subgroup reading carrying no between-class test' (and claim_b): there is indeed no between-class test, but P-1157 reports adjusted per-category Cox estimates, antihypertensive agents HR 0.59 (0.37-0.93) and lipid-modifying agents HR 0.43 (0.23-0.79). The record omits them, although they are the figures a synthesis would set against P-999's class-level HRs.

residual_risk says P-999's class-level HRs are 'reported with no confidence intervals anywhere in its digest', so that the estimate 'rests on sample size alone'. The PDF prints a 95% CI for every class-level aHR (Table 3).
'a corpus estimate 600 times larger in sample': 128,683 / 237 is about 543.

The evidence quote filed under P-999 ('The results nominate common antihypertensive, statin and metformin combinations for formal drug-repurposing trials, but do not establish treatment efficacy') and claim_a's 'its own significance statement declines efficacy' have no counterpart in the PDF: there is no such sentence and no significance statement. The authors conclude that 'All five major AHM classes showed a protective effect' and ask only that the associations 'be interpreted with caution and warrant replication'.
The gate FAIL on modality_subtype rests on P-1157 being coded 'nomogram_clinical_scores', but P-1157 builds no nomogram. This concerns registry state, not a PDF contradiction.

papers_read.title_as_printed: Associations of Antihypertensive Medication Consumption and Drug-Drug Interaction with Statin and Metformin with Reduced Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Risk among Hypertensive Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment using High Volume Claims Data
Polypharmacy and risk of dementia progression in older adults with mild cognitive impairment: A longitudinal cohort study

challenge.by: second model reader instructed to argue the verdict into a genuine contradiction (or out of one), reading both source documents in full
challenge.strongest_case_against_the_verdict: P-1157's Figure 3 shows 'Antihypertensive Drugs' as one pooled category, so its HR 0.59 (0.37-0.93) carries the same label as P-999's any-AHM-vs-none aHR 1.06 (1.04-1.08): antihypertensive use vs non-use in older adults with MCI, all-cause dementia, adjusted Cox HR. The directions are opposite, each interval excludes 1 and the intervals are disjoint, which meets the brief's reading of 'incompatible'. Task (T2), validation tier (n/a: two association studies) and modality family (medication-exposure records) match. The dataset-family mismatch is what independent replication looks like, and a cohort difference was waived before (C-232). On this reading, P-999's restriction to hypertensives is a narrower sample of the same population class: 65% of P-1157 is hypertensive and its antihypertensive users are predominantly hypertensive. P-1157's missing hypertension covariate would then be a confounding weakness in P-1157, a reason to doubt one estimate rather than a reason to call them different quantities. Treating every difference in adjustment set as a different quantity would make no two observational studies comparable, which is exactly the external critic's objection.
challenge.why_it_does_or_does_not_succeed: The case fails on the comparison, not on the gate. P-999 restricts on the exposure's own indication, so 'non-user' denotes a different clinical state in each study: an untreated hypertensive in P-999 (28,005 of 128,683), and mostly a participant without hypertension in P-1157 (at least 83 of 237, with no hypertension term in the model). P-999's authors restricted the cohort for exactly this reason: including normotensives 'would add a potential confounder (hypertension status) that could not be well controlled as very few normotensive patients are taking AHMs'. P-1157's own counts show why this matters. From Table 2, 47 of 154 hypertensive participants progressed (30.5%) against 42 of 83 without hypertension (50.6%), a crude ratio of about 0.60, the same size as the adjusted antihypertensive HR of 0.59. Nothing in P-1157 separates the two associations. Both reported results can therefore hold at once: hypertension status goes with slower progression in the Kaohsiung cohort, while treated and untreated hypertensives in Optum differ little. The pair passes the incompatibility test only if the two quantities are treated as one, and they are not one. Co-medication is a second difference. P-999's estimate for the same labelled contrast is 0.84 (0.80-0.88) with statins and 1.11 (1.08-1.13) without. P-1157 conditions on no co-medication, although its lipid-modifying agents carry HR 0.43, and its interval contains P-999's statin-user estimate, so on one plausible alignment the numbers are even compatible. This is not a confounding critique relabelled: the reference category is a different population, and two studies sharing that population and comparator could still contradict each other. The first reader's dataset-family ground is the weakest of their five; a waiver would be reasonable here, and the verdict does not need that ground. A waiver still cannot cure a comparator difference (the C-232/C-80 reasoning). I checked all ten first-reader quotes on their cited pages (all verbatim) and every number in their file against the PDFs, and found no factual error. I also checked P-999's stratum labels. The Table 5 footnote and Figure 1 give the statin-user stratum as N = 59,980, whereas Table 1 gives 68,703 statin users. The interval widths fit Table 1's strata (0.80-0.88 rests on only 3,029 statin-using non-users), so the labels are swapped, not the estimates, and the first reader's reading of 0.84 as the statin-user figure stands. No corpus study bridges the pair on a common quantity: P-1002 reports average treatment effects, not hazard ratios, in an unrestricted EHR cohort.
grounds: Exposure contrast: P-999 compares hypertensive MCI patients who consumed any antihypertensive during the study period with hypertensive MCI patients who took none; P-1157 compares MCI participants with a baseline prescription in its pooled 'Antihypertensive Drugs' category against participants without one, most of whom have no hypertension.

Population: P-999 is 128,683 US claimants restricted by design to hypertension, with a first MCI diagnosis at a mean age of about 76; P-1157 is 237 Taiwanese veterans aged over 60 at CDR 0.5, 65% (154/237) of them hypertensive.

Outcome and horizon: P-999 counts claims-coded ADRD or a second anti-dementia fill, followed to the last encounter (mean about 22 months to ADRD among converters); P-1157 counts neurologist-confirmed CDR 1 at annual visits over a median 34 months; both are all-cause dementia, and this difference alone would be tolerable.

Adjustment set: P-999 adjusts for age, sex, race, 13 comorbidities and statin and metformin use, and holds hypertension constant by restriction; P-1157 adjusts for age, sex, CCI, education, smoking, sensory impairment, Barthel, GDS-15, MNA-SF and recruitment source, with no hypertension or co-medication term.

The dataset-family, ascertainment and horizon mismatches are gate-level differences that could reasonably be waived for two independent pharmacoepidemiologic cohorts, so the verdict does not rest on them.

The comparator is not waivable: it differs in kind (untreated hypertensives vs mostly normotensives), and P-999's authors name this as the reason they excluded normotensives, so the two HRs are different estimands, not two estimates of one estimand separated by a gate.

P-1157's hypertension-status association (30.5% vs 50.6% progression, crude ratio about 0.60, derived from Table 2) is the size of its antihypertensive HR (0.59), so its estimate cannot be separated from hypertension status and both papers' results can be true together.

P-999's estimate for the same labelled contrast runs from 0.84 (0.80-0.88) with statins to 1.11 (1.08-1.13) without, and P-1157's interval contains the former, so without a co-medication-matched P-1157 estimate no pairing is incompatible on a common quantity.

The record's own framing (class-level 0.96-0.98 against a medication-count HR of 0.49) sets different exposures against each other, as the first reader found, so the verdict holds on every alignment of the two papers' estimates.

unresolved_discrepancy_2026_09_30.summary: Two cohort studies of older adults with MCI disagree on antihypertensive use and progression to dementia. Among 128,683 hypertensive US claims patients (P-999), any antihypertensive use against none carried an adjusted HR of 1.06 (95% CI 1.04-1.08). Among 237 Taiwanese veterans (P-1157), baseline antihypertensive exposure carried an HR of 0.59 (0.37-0.93). The difference is beyond combined uncertainty (z = 2.49, log scale). P-999 compares treated with untreated hypertensives and adjusts for statin and metformin use, while P-1157's unexposed group includes normotensive patients. P-999's own statin-user stratum (0.84, 0.80-0.88) does not differ from P-1157 beyond uncertainty (z = 1.50). These differences are candidate explanations, none shown to be sufficient.
candidate_explanations: Population and reference group: P-999 is restricted to hypertensive MCI, so its comparator is untreated hypertensives, and it excluded normotensives because hypertension status 'could not be well controlled'. P-1157 includes normotensives and has no hypertension covariate; its progressors had less hypertension (p = 0.003). Crude progression is 30.5% (47/154) in hypertensives against 50.6% (42/83) in normotensives, a ratio of 0.60, close to the HR of 0.59.

Co-medication: P-999 adjusts for statin and metformin use, and its any-AHM estimate reverses with statin co-use (0.84 with, 1.11 without). P-1157's per-category models adjust for no other drug, and lipid-modifying agents are separately protective there (HR 0.43).
Exposure window: baseline prescription records (P-1157) against use 'during the study period' (P-999).
Outcome ascertainment: claims-based ADRD (P-999) against CDR 0.5 to 1, confirmed by neurologists (P-1157).
Setting and size: US Optum claims, N = 128,683 (a preprint), against Taiwanese veterans' homes and a hospital outpatient clinic, N = 237.
Multiplicity: P-1157's estimate is one of 15 exploratory per-category models, tested at p < 0.05 without correction.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
