challenge.by: second model reader instructed to argue the verdict into a genuine contradiction (or out of one), reading both source documents in full
challenge.strongest_case_against_the_verdict: Set P-1407's MCI-AD subgroup, the part of the Newcastle cohort closest to BALTAZAR (P-1267 excluded Lewy body, parkinsonian, frontotemporal and vascular MCI, and 96% of its converters went to probable AD), against P-1267's continuous ratio. P-1407 gives HR 0.67 (0.37-1.20) per control-referenced SD of the inverted ratio, so a more abnormal (lower) Abeta42/40 goes with a LOWER hazard. P-1267 gives HR 0.95 (0.91-0.99) for the free ratio and 0.92 (0.86-0.98) for the total ratio per percentage point, so a lower ratio goes with a HIGHER hazard. Put P-1267 on a per-SD scale using its own printed sample SDs (free 20.4 +/- 7.3, total 13.9 +/- 4.5 percentage points, Table 2): per SD lower ratio, about 1.45 (1.08-1.99) free and 1.46 (1.10-1.97) total (my computation). On that scale P-1407's MCI-AD interval excludes P-1267's point estimate, P-1267's interval excludes P-1407's point estimate, and a z-test of the difference in log hazard ratios gives z of about 2.3 (p of about 0.02). The dataset-family mismatch (Newcastle vs BALTAZAR) could plausibly be waived on the C-232 precedent, which waived a cross-cohort difference. Read as 'a point estimate outside the other study's interval', this is an incompatibility on a quantity the ledger record never named.
challenge.why_it_does_or_does_not_succeed: It does not succeed under the rule as written. (1) The rescaled intervals still overlap (P-1407 0.37-1.20 against P-1267 from 1.08 or 1.10 upward), and they keep overlapping unless one Newcastle control SD on the Simoa scale corresponded to more than about two BALTAZAR MCI-sample SDs on the INNO-BIA scale (about 2.0 for the total ratio, 2.5 for the free ratio), which nothing in either paper suggests. CONFLICT_BRIEF says significant vs non-significant 'with overlapping intervals' is not incompatible, so 'reported uncertainty excludes the other' cannot be met by a point estimate falling outside the other interval while the intervals overlap. (2) P-1407's MCI-AD direction has no support from its own statistics (p = 0.180), so the 'opposite directions each supported by the study's own statistics' limb fails. (3) The per-SD scale is my construction, not reported uncertainty: P-1407 standardises blood results to the control mean without printing the control SD, uses another platform (Simoa, against INNO-BIA free and total fractions) and inverts the ratio; no interval printed by either paper excludes the other. The z-test is a heterogeneity test the rule does not use, and it is fragile: its p-value rises to about 0.06 if the control SD is half the BALTAZAR SD, and to about 0.07 with P-1267's unadjusted estimate. (4) The covariate-conditional estimands differ in a way that bears on the result: P-1267's continuous association is significant only with APOE e4 in the model (unadjusted free ratio HR 0.97, 0.93-1.02, p = 0.21, about 1.25, 0.87-1.70, per SD), whereas P-1407 adjusts for MMSE. In BALTAZAR itself, MMSE predicts conversion strongly (HR 0.85 per point, p = 0.0002) and was higher in the top quartile of the total ratio (p = 0.046); P-1267 prints no MMSE-adjusted model. (5) The endpoints differ: P-1407 uses dementia or death with no fixed horizon; P-1267 uses adjudicated dementia, censored at 36 months or the last visit. In addition, P-1407's MCI-AD group is assigned from the final diagnosis after follow-up (n = 43, 21 events). (6) The whole-cohort (1.06) and probable MCI-LB (1.23) estimates point the same way as P-1267, and their intervals overlap P-1267's on any scaling. The other alternative, documented_incommensurability, rests on the operator's C-234 reclassification, which listed 'different quantities' before 'compatible results'. It does not displace false_positive: CONFLICT_BRIEF applies false_positive first, and two of its limbs are met. The results are compatible (the difference is one of significance), and the record misreads P-1407 (it calls the 72 dementia-or-death events conversions, treats non-significant hazard ratios as 'no prognostic value', and its review note says no HR, CI or p-value exists). Either way the pair is not genuine. The first reader's grounds stand; I add the rescaling test above because it is the obvious counter-argument and the verdict survives it. The first reader's hypothetical item (d), the dataset-family gate, is the weakest of their four incommensurability items because a cross-cohort waiver has precedent (C-232), but items (a) to (c) carry that hypothetical without it.
grounds: P-1407 prints Abeta42/40 hazard ratios for all three groups, and with the ratio inverted so that higher means more abnormal, the whole-cohort (1.06, 0.83-1.35) and probable MCI-LB (1.23, 0.94-1.60) estimates point the same way as P-1267's protective high ratio.
The only opposite estimate, MCI-AD 0.67 (0.37-1.20, p = 0.180), is not supported by P-1407's own statistics, so no pair of opposite directions is each statistically supported.

Rescaled with P-1267's own printed sample SDs, P-1267's continuous hazard ratios (about 1.45 per SD lower ratio, lower limits about 1.08 to 1.10) overlap P-1407's MCI-AD interval under any plausible scaling, so the rule's overlapping-intervals clause makes this a difference in significance, not an incompatibility.

P-1267's continuous association depends on APOE e4 adjustment (unadjusted free ratio HR 0.97, 0.93-1.02, p = 0.21), whereas P-1407 adjusts for MMSE, which strongly predicts conversion in BALTAZAR itself, so the covariate-conditional estimands differ.

The endpoints differ (dementia or death in P-1407; adjudicated dementia censored at 36 months in P-1267), and P-1407's MCI-AD group is assigned from the final diagnosis after follow-up, while BALTAZAR excluded non-AD MCI at baseline.
The record misreads P-1407: its 72 events are dementia-or-death events, not conversions, and its non-significant hazard ratios are recast as 'no prognostic value'.
The dataset-family gate fails with no waiver on record; a waiver on the C-232 precedent is conceivable but would not cure the grounds above.

readjudication_2026_09_27.by: model reader delegated by the operator in session on 2026-09-27 (instruction: 'Read both source PDFs of each pair against the existing rule, unchanged; a second agent checks any genuine verdict'); both source documents read in full; rule of Appendix H.1 of literature_review.md, unchanged
readjudication_2026_09_27.quantity_a: Pooled SMD of CSF YKL-40, AD minus any-MCI (clinical diagnosis by international criteria), random effects, 15 observational studies published to May 2025.
readjudication_2026_09_27.quantity_b: Pooled difference in CSF YKL-40, AD minus 'MCI' (stable MCI per the abstract), random effects, 7 case-control studies from 1990 to October 2021; stated as an SMD but apparently an unstandardised mean difference. Separately, AD minus MCI-AD (progressive MCI), fixed effects, 5 studies.
grounds: On the one comparison both papers report, CSF YKL-40 AD vs MCI, the point estimates agree in direction. P-1427 gives SMD 0.25 (-0.08 to 0.57), which it calls 'an increasing trend'. P-1337 says YKL-40 was 'significantly increased in AD patients compared to MCI patients'.

The difference is in significance only, and P-1337's side is itself marginal: z = 2.02, p = 0.0429, seven studies, I2 = 97.4%. Section 5.2 says 'a difference in statistical significance between two of them is not a data conflict'. The operator reached the same reading for C-234 (compatible results; 'the difference is one of precision, not direction').

P-1337's strongly significant AD vs MCI-AD result (z = 7.68, fixed effects) and its MCI-AD vs stable MCI result concern progressive MCI, which P-1427 never separates. Setting them against P-1427's any-MCI null would set a claim about X against a claim about Y.

The papers' opposite interpretive conclusions follow from that significance difference, not from opposite data. P-1337 proposes YKL-40 for 'the differential diagnosis between AD and MCI'; P-1427 stresses 'its limited ability to differentiate between MCI and AD'. P-1427 presents its null as an update of earlier, smaller meta-analyses and cites P-1337 as reference 7.

P-1427's reporting of this comparison is internally inconsistent: p = 0.134, 0.12 and 0.53 are all printed, and its Table 4 repeats Table 2's values with every subgroup significant. This weakens its null further and cannot turn it into a result in the opposite direction.

record_defects: review_note issue 1 says 'P-1337 narrates CSF YKL-40 studies 1990-2021'. The PDF pools them quantitatively, printing z, p, I2 and tau2 for each comparison, with forest and funnel plots, Egger's tests and NOS scoring (pp.2, 4-8).

review_note issue 3 relies on P-1337's block calling it a 'Narrative review, not a formal ...' synthesis, and the block adds 'no pooled effect sizes with CIs'. The PDF pools effects and plots them with 95% confidence intervals, although the plots are images.

conflict_statement frames the pair as P-1427 'does not differ significantly' against P-1337 'significantly higher'. Both PDFs place AD above MCI; the record does not state that P-1427's point estimate is positive or that P-1337's AD-vs-MCI result is marginal (z = 2.02, p = 0.0429, I2 = 97.4%).

conflict_statement 'significantly higher in AD than in both MCI-AD and stable MCI' takes the abstract's label. The results section names the 7-study comparison only 'mild cognitive impairment' (p.7), so the stable-MCI reading comes from the abstract, not from a separately reported pooling.

summary.audit_note_2026_09_14: Summary counters recomputed from live record state on 2026-09-14 (audit; not a gate). The previous block was incremented rather than recomputed - the 2026-09-09 commit message claimed 'refreshed to live values' but only total_conflicts, pending_review and with_g4_reviewed_true matched. Formula per key, all computed over the 201 records in the conflicts array: total_conflicts = len(conflicts) = 201 (was 197; the four 2026-09-04 frontier candidates C-264..C-267 were never counted). with_genuine_conflict_field = records carrying a 'genuine_conflict' key = 181 (20 legacy records - C-153..C-155, C-188..C-203, C-233 - have none). with_g4_reviewed_true = records with g4_reviewed === true = 145. pending_review = records with status == 'pending_human_review' = 17 (C-242, C-248, C-253..C-267). genuine_conflict_breakdown = counts of the stored representations of the older 'genuine' field, each counted separately because the field holds booleans, strings and absences: genuine_true (literal true) 4, genuine_yes_string ('Yes') 1, genuine_false (literal false) 89, genuine_no_string ('No') 29, genuine_null (key absent or null) 74, genuine_partial 0, plus a new genuine_other_strings key = 4 (the four C-264..C-267 records store the string 'pending_human_review' in 'genuine'); the seven sub-counts sum to total_conflicts. genuine_conflicts / partial_conflicts / not_genuine_conflicts = 5 / 0 / 196, computed with the pipeline's own rule in agent4_relational._refresh_conflicts_summary (take genuine_conflict, else genuine, else false; truthy bool or 'yes'/'true' counts genuine, 'partial' counts partial, everything else counts not-genuine). The genuine set is exactly C-80, C-204, C-227, C-232, C-234. The previous values (7 / 0 / 164) matched neither field and did not sum to the total. total_records = total_conflicts = 201 (the two keys have always been the same quantity; the old 171 was a pre-2026-08 archive count). confirmed_conflicts = genuine AND carrying an operator confirmation marker (gate_verified true, or review_status starting 'confirmed', or resolution_status in {genuine_confirmed, genuine_conflict_confirmed, confirmed_human_g4}, or status 'genuine_confirmed') = 4: C-80 and C-204 (status genuine_confirmed), C-227 (review_status confirmed_human_g4_2026-07-31) and C-232 (gate_verified true). The fifth genuine record, C-234, is resolution_status 'open_genuine' with no confirmation marker, which is why confirmed_conflicts is one below genuine_conflicts. average_performance_gap_percentage = mean of the 145 numeric gap_magnitude fields x 100 = 17.457. task_equivalence_rate / dataset_equivalence_rate / validation_comparability_rate = share of truthy values among the records that carry task_equal (158 records), dataset_equal (158) and validation_comparable (151) respectively; the three were previously all printed as 0.892, which is not reproducible from any of the three columns. Unchanged by this recomputation: inflated_performance_flags and every dated narrative note, which are history rather than counters.
